scope_description: Everything since the last approved review point (56b437aa, the worktree-concurrency-guard independent review's own close commit, 2 P1s fixed and delta-reviewed) through the current HEAD (56d9f8ad): the bee 1.18.2 merge/port (cell port-1, feature worktree-concurrency-guard-controlroot-port) that relocated the shared-nested-checkout concurrency guard to packages/bee/ and threaded controlRoot scoping through it, plus its scribing sync commit.
head: 56d9f8ad

reviewers.trigger: packages/bee/bee.mjs is a public CLI surface (handleWorktreeNew)
live-session/concurrency detection across worktrees, external git state reads

findings.summary: Hardcoded 'AGENTS.md rule 14' reference in the user-facing refusal is a stable-looking anchor that will drift on renumber.
controlRoot plumbing in handleWorktreeNew is inert on every CLI-reachable path (ctrlRoot===mainRoot always); correct by design, flagged for documentation only.
Duplicate test-row numbering (70-71 reused) in test_write_guard.mjs.
Tests import the guard primitives from the vendored copy, not source; correct existing convention, flagged as a standing property.

Stale comment at guards.mjs claiming the shared-nested-checkout primitive is 'deliberately NOT wired into checkWrite or the hook dispatch yet' -- it is now wired; a maintainer could misread this as unenforced and remove the wiring.
Duplicate row-number labels (70/71) reused across two distinct test blocks in test_write_guard.mjs.
hasAnySharedNestedCheckout's shape-(a) verified-companion-mount branch is never exercised via the directory-scan entry point.
Directory-scan submodule exclusion + skip-dirs (node_modules etc.) + max-depth bound are untested at the scan-path invocation.
apply_patch writes are not fed to the shared-nested check -- confirmed pre-existing (not a port regression), already scoped out in wcg-2's own report; no test documents the boundary.
controlRoot === '' collapses to root via the || fallback, untested at the primitive level; low risk today since callers never pass empty string.
Duplicate row-number labels (cosmetic, same as architecture/code-quality's finding).

docs/history walkthrough.md for the original feature still documents the dropped typed [WORKTREE_CONCURRENT_SHARED_NESTED] error-code prefix, which Port-D7 replaced with a plain Error -- a manual repro following the doc would see mismatched output.
bee.mjs header comment slightly overstates the WorktreeCreateError situation -- true only scoped to handleWorktreeNew, but createFeatureWorktree still emits [CODE]-prefixed refusals via that class.

F1: isConcurrentMode/listSessionRecords swallowed every fs error identically to a legitimately-missing sessions directory, so a transient hard error (EACCES/EIO/EMFILE) during the concurrency check silently read as 'nobody else is live' and ALLOWED the write -- fail-open regression of the guard's own documented fail-closed contract, widened by controlRoot potentially pointing at a shared/remote coordination root.

F2: the structural filesystem helpers (realpathOrNull, hasGitNode, scanForNestedCheckout's readdir, resolveVerifiedCompanionMountReal, isRegisteredSubmodule) had the same swallow-everything pattern; pre-existing from the original (non-port) feature, out of this port's declared scope per the reviewer's own note, but fixed anyway per user request.
F3: controlRoot resolution failure fails closed in bee.mjs (throw before any mutation) but falls back to root (mild narrowing, not a new bug) in the hook via the existing || root fallback.

F4: vendor drift is only caught in the source-to-vendored direction by onboard_bee.mjs's status check; currently verified clean (sha256 match), residual risk is a future hand-edit of the vendored copy going unnoticed.

Residual same-defect-class gap the F1 fix did not reach: listSessionRecords' per-record read (readSession -> readJson) still swallowed a hard error on ONE specific session file even under strict mode -- narrower window than F1 (needs readdir-success + specific-file-failure) but same fail-open shape.

The dedicated security reviewer slot failed to produce a report twice (review-security, review-security-2) despite repeated direct pings -- appears to be a systemic dispatch/delivery issue, not findings-related. Security-relevant properties for this change (self-exclusion, fail-closed-on-detection-error, controlRoot as a bypass surface) were nonetheless independently verified via: the reliability reviewer's explicit fail-open/fail-closed analysis (F1-F4), the delta re-review of the F1/F2 fix, and this orchestrator's own cross-model (opus) semantic-judge goal-check performed before this review session. No P1 surfaced in any of these. User was informed and chose to proceed with synthesis rather than a third dispatch attempt.

Submodule exclusion trusts .gitmodules content -- an agent able to write .gitmodules could register a shared nested checkout as a fake submodule to bypass the guard. By design (D2's registration discriminator); threat model is accidental concurrent clobbering, not a deliberate adversary.

Corrupt/leftover session record can fail-closed a genuinely solo worktree-new/write under strict mode -- intended posture (undetectable state must not read as solo), safe-direction availability edge, not a security regression.

payload.session_id absent weakens self-exclusion in the write-guard (excludeSessionId becomes null) -- can only over-deny (fail-closed), and a sessionless caller typically writes no heartbeat anyway, so isConcurrentMode usually returns false regardless. Informational, not a regression.

uat.item: bee worktree new --feature x (no --with-companion) refuses with a clear message naming --with-companion as the fix, zero mutation, while another session is concurrently live over a shared nested checkout; re-running with --with-companion succeeds.
uat.note: User accepted based on automated evidence (87+20 test rows incl. both original P1 regression guards, 6 independent reviewers) rather than a manual repro.

gate4.note: Update (2026-07-26, later same session): the security reviewer slot succeeded on a 4th attempt, dispatched synchronously (foreground) rather than as a background/mailbox-relayed agent, after 3 consecutive background dispatches (2x general-purpose 'claude' type, 1x 'bee-review' type) all went idle without ever delivering report text despite repeated direct pings. Security review: 0 P1, 0 P2, 3 P3 (all advisory/no_change_needed -- submodule-registration trust, corrupt-record fail-closed-availability edge, sessionless self-exclusion note). All 7 reviewer lenses (code-quality, architecture, test-coverage, api-contract, reliability, security, plus the delta re-review) now complete with 0 P1 total. gate_bypass_level=total; P1=0 and the sole UAT item was human-confirmed pass, satisfying the bypass merge-approval precondition.
